almond-biscotti.note: Ours is leaner than Once Upon a Chef's butter version (2 1/2 cups flour, 10 tbsp butter, 2 eggs) and richer than the egg-only Italian style (2 cups flour, 3 eggs, no butter), which suits a crunchy dunking biscotti. Logs at 350°F for 25–30 minutes, then slices dried at 325°F, match the sources.

aloo-gobi.note: Onion, ginger and ground spices, then potatoes and cauliflower with tomatoes and a little water covered 15-20 min, then uncovered to dry and brown; published covered times are 15-25 min. No change.

apple-cinnamon-muffins.note: 2 cups flour with 2 1/2 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs, melted butter and milk, plus diced apple and a melted-butter streusel, at 400°F for 18–22 minutes. This matches published streusel muffins (about 2 cups flour, 2–3 tsp baking powder, 400°F).

apple-crisp.note: 6 apples in a 9-inch square under an oat topping (1 c oats, 3/4 c flour, 3/4 c brown sugar, 1/2 c butter), 350°F for 40-45 min: matches published crisps (350°F, 40-45 min in an 8- to 9-inch pan).

apple-turnovers.note: Precooked apple filling thickened with cornstarch and fully cooled, puff pastry squares folded and sealed, egg wash, a short chill, then 400°F for 20–25 minutes. This matches published versions (400°F, 16–30 minutes).

arroz-a-la-cubana.note: Matches the Spanish version: garlic white rice, homemade fried tomato sauce, fried egg and fried banana, with no meat. arroz-con-pollo.note: 2 cups long-grain rice with 2 1/2 cups broth plus 8 oz tomato sauce (about 1.75 to 1) with browned bone-in thighs, 25-30 min covered plus a 10-min rest. Published ratios run from about 1.25 to 1 (Cook's Country) to 2 to 1 (VICE), and ATK also keeps a splash of water in reserve. No change.

asian-chicken-salad-with-sesame-dressing.note: Rice vinegar, soy, honey, sesame oil, ginger and neutral oil dressing over napa and red cabbage with chicken pounded to 3/4 inch and cooked to 165°F. Matches the published formula.

avgolemono.note: 8 cups broth, 2/3 cup rice, 3 eggs and 1/2 cup lemon juice, tempered with 2 cups of hot broth and kept below a boil. Sources use 8 cups broth, 2/3–1 cup rice, 2–4 eggs or yolks and the same tempering. In line.

avocado-toast-with-fried-egg.note: Avocado mashed with lemon and salt on toast, topped with a 2–3 minute fried egg, is the standard build.

baba-ganoush.note: 2 lb eggplant broiled until collapsed and drained, with 1/4 cup tahini and about 3 tbsp lemon: matches published ratios (1/4 cup tahini and 1/4 cup lemon per 2 lb) and the char-then-drain method.

baked-apple-dumplings.note: Whole cored apples wrapped in double-crust-size pastry, baked in a water/brown sugar/butter syrup; published versions run 400-425F then 350F for 40-50 min, and our 15 min at 425F then 35-40 min at 350F with a skewer test fits.

baked-pesto-salmon-with-green-beans.note: 425°F: green beans and tomatoes get a head start of 8 minutes, then the pesto-panko salmon roasts 12–15 minutes to 145°F. Sources roast pesto salmon with green beans at 425°F for 12–15 minutes. In line.

baked-potato-bar-with-chili-and-cheddar.note: Our potatoes, oiled, salted and pricked russets baked on the rack at 425°F for 50–60 minutes, match The Kitchn exactly; ATK uses 450°F for 45–60. The quick beef and bean chili is simmered thick and the beef is cooked to 160°F.

baked-ziti-with-beef.note: 1 lb ziti, 1 lb beef in about 6 cups of tomato sauce, ricotta pockets and 12 oz mozzarella in a 9x13, baked at 375°F for 20 minutes under foil plus 15–20 uncovered. Sources use 12–16 oz pasta in 9x13 and bake 25–40 minutes at 375°F. In line.

bakewell-tart.note: The frangipane is roughly equal weights of butter, sugar and ground almonds (113/100/100 g) with 2 eggs and a little flour, the classic proportion (Baking Mad: 125/125/125 g, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tbsp flour). Blind-baked sweet shortcrust and a jam layer match. 30–35 minutes at 350°F has a toothpick check.

banana-pudding.note: Custard of 3 cups milk, 1/4 cup cornstarch and 4 yolks boiled 1 min matches scratch versions (3 cups milk with 3 yolks and 3 tbsp cornstarch plus flour); layering and 4 h chill are standard.

bangers-and-mash-with-onion-gravy.note: Gravy uses 1 1/2 tbsp flour to 1 1/2 cups broth over slow-cooked onions. Published versions use about 2 tsp to 1 tbsp flour per 1–1.5 cups of stock, so ours is on the thicker side but in range. Sausages cooked to 160°F and the mash are standard.

banh-mi-sandwiches.note: Quick pickle of equal vinegar and water with sugar and salt (published: similar vinegar-water-sugar brine, at least 30-60 min), thin pork tenderloin marinated in fish sauce and sugar and seared to 145°F, crisped baguette. No change.

bbq-chicken-pizza.note: 1 lb dough on a sheet pan, 2 cups mozzarella, bottom rack at 475°F for 12-15 min; published sheet-pan versions bake at 450-500°F for 13-15 min. No change.

bean-and-cheese-pupusas-with-curtido.note: 3 cups masa harina to 2 1/4 cups warm water is a ratio of 0.75, inside the published 0.67-0.9, and the dough is adjusted by feel. They cook 4-5 min a side, and the curtido is pickled in vinegar.

beef-and-barley-soup.note: Chef Dennis also uses 1 1/2 lb of chuck in 8 cups of beef broth for about 2 hours. Others simmer the beef about 1 hour, then cook the pearl barley 45–60 minutes. Our 3/4 cup of barley and 1 hour plus 45–50 minutes match.

beef-and-bean-chili.note: 1 1/2 lb beef, 3 tbsp chili powder, two cans beans, 28 oz tomatoes and a 30-minute simmer are all in the range of published beef-and-bean chilis (2-3 tbsp chili powder, 30 min simmer).

beef-and-black-bean-enchiladas.note: The roux sauce is 3 tbsp oil, 3 tbsp flour and 3 tbsp chili powder to 3 cups broth, plus tomato paste. Sources use 2–4 tbsp flour to 2 cups. Ours is a little thinner, but it is simmered and then baked uncovered, which suits enchiladas. The filling, the 20 minutes at 375°F and the step that softens the tortillas are all standard.

beef-and-mushroom-pie.note: Floured chuck braised with mushrooms in red wine and broth for 1 1/2–2 hours. The filling cools before the puff pastry goes on, then bakes at 400°F for 25–30 minutes. Sources braise about 1 3/4–2 hours and bake at 200°C for 30–35 minutes. In line.

beef-and-spinach-stuffed-pasta-shells.note: 24 jumbo shells filled with beef, spinach, ricotta and egg, with 3 cups marinara, baked at 375°F for 25 minutes under foil plus 10–15 uncovered. Sources use the same 3 cups of sauce and bake 20 minutes covered plus 10–15 uncovered at 375°F. In line.

beef-bulgogi.note: 1 1/2 lb thin-sliced ribeye in soy, brown sugar (3 tbsp, as JOC), grated apple (JOC's stated pear substitute), garlic and sesame oil, partly frozen to slice, marinated 30 min to 8 h and seared in batches. In range.

beef-empanadas.note: Dough is 3 cups flour, 1 stick butter, 1 egg and about 1/2 cup water. Published baked doughs use 1 to 1 1/2 sticks per 2 1/4–3 cups flour, so ours is leaner and less flaky but still a workable empanada dough. Liquid and the 400°F, 20–25 minute bake are in range. The filling (picadillo with olives and chopped egg) cools before filling and makes enough for 12.

beef-kofta-with-yogurt-sauce.note: Beef with grated, squeezed onion, parsley, cumin and coriander, shaped into 2 oz logs and broiled 9–10 minutes to 160°F. Sources broil thinner skewered kofta 6–7 minutes. Our logs are thicker, and the thermometer cue covers the difference. Sound.

beef-tips-and-gravy-over-rice.note: Published versions braise chuck about 2 hours on the stove in a broth gravy thickened with flour, and so does ours (1 1/2–2 hours, with a step to reduce or thin the gravy). Rice at 1 1/2 cups to 2 3/4 cups of water is fine.

beer-battered-fish-and-chips.note: Batter of 1 cup flour to 1 cup beer with baking powder (Rouxbe uses the same 1:1; Donna Hay about 225 g flour to 375 ml). Chips are fried at 325°F, then at 375°F, and the thick cod for 5–7 minutes at 375°F. Published fish times run 3–7 minutes at 350–375°F depending on thickness, so ours is at the long end for thick fillets, with a 145°F check.

beer-battered-onion-rings.note: Rings dusted in flour, then dipped in a batter of roughly equal flour and beer, and fried 2–3 minutes at 375°F in 2 inches of oil. This matches the published method, ratio and temperature.

bibimbap-with-spinach-and-fried-egg.note: Rinsed short-grain rice at about 1:1.17 water, a little drier, as the sources advise for bibimbap. Spinach is blanched 30 s and sprouts 1-2 min, and the gochujang sauce is 3 tbsp with sugar, vinegar and sesame oil, inside the published range.

black-bean-and-corn-salad.note: Two cans of beans, 2–3 cups of corn and a lime, oil and cumin dressing is the standard ratio. Our 3 tbsp oil to the juice of 2 limes is in line with it.

black-bean-and-egg-breakfast-bowls-with-.note: Cumin and garlic black beans simmered and partly mashed, lime-cilantro rice, fresh pico and a fried egg. Matches published black bean breakfast bowls, and the quantities suit 4.

black-bean-and-rice-burritos.note: 1 cup rice to 1 3/4 cups water sits inside the published 1:1.5 to 1:2. The beans are cooked with spices, and toasting the rolled burritos on a griddle is a published step.

black-bean-and-sweet-potato-enchiladas.note: The roux sauce has 1 tbsp flour per cup of broth (published 1-1.5). Chili powder at 1.3 tbsp per cup is a little above the usual 1, but that is a matter of taste. The 12 corn tortillas, 9x13 dish and 375F bake (covered, then uncovered) are standard.

black-bean-burgers.note: 2 cans beans : 3/4 cup panko : 1 egg is the same ratio as other oven-dried versions (This Healthy Table), and published ranges run 3/4 to 1 cup panko and 1 to 2 eggs (ATK uses 2 eggs, but its beans aren't dried). black-bean-chili-with-bell-peppers.note: 3 cans of black beans, a 28-oz can of tomatoes, chipotle in adobo and a 25-30 min simmer, the same as the published vegetarian black bean chilis.

black-bean-quesadillas.note: Mashed spiced beans and cheddar in folded flour tortillas, 2-3 min per side over medium: matches published skillet quesadillas; 1 1/2 cups cheese for 4 large tortillas is normal.

black-bean-soup.note: Published versions use about 1 cup of broth per can of beans (4 and 4, or 3 and 3), simmer about 20 minutes and blend half. Ours does the same: 4 cans, 4 cups, 25 minutes, half blended.

blt-sandwich.note: The Kitchn gives about 18 minutes for thick-cut bacon at 400°F and ATK about 13–16, so our 15–20 minutes with a visual cue is in range. The assembly is the classic one.

blueberry-crumb-bars.note: Works as written: 9x13, 375F, ~45 min. bobotie.note: 2 lb beef with curry powder, milk-soaked bread, jam, raisins and lemon, under a custard of 3 eggs and 1 cup milk with bay leaves, baked at 350F. The beef is fully cooked on the stove first (to 160F), so the 30-35 min bake only has to set the custard; published versions that bake raw meat take about an hour.

broccoli-and-cheddar-stuffed-baked-potat.note: 10-oz russets bake 50-60 min at 425F (published: 40-75 min at 425F), then the filled shells bake again for 15-20 min (published 20-25). The butter, sour cream, milk and cheddar filling is standard.

broccoli-and-egg-fried-rice.note: 4 cups chilled rice, 4 eggs and 2 1/2 tbsp soy for 3 servings is inside the published 4–5 cups rice and 0.5–3 tbsp soy. Cooking the eggs first and broccoli separately is sound.

broccoli-cheddar-ranch-pasta-salad.note: 12 oz pasta with broccoli blanched in the pasta pot and cubed cheddar, in about 1 3/4 cups homemade ranch (mayonnaise, sour cream, buttermilk, herbs), part of it held back for serving. Proportions and method are in line with published ranch pasta salads.

broccoli-cheddar-soup.note: Roux of 4 tbsp butter and 1/4 cup flour for 4 cups liquid with 8 oz cheddar: matches Smitten Kitchen (same roux for 5 cups, 2 1/2 cups cheddar) and Fine Dining Lovers (2 oz each for 4 cups, 8 oz cheese). Cheese is added off the boil, correctly.

broccoli-pesto-pasta.note: Blanched broccoli blended with toasted walnuts (1/3 cup, as in Fake Ginger), basil, garlic, Parmesan, lemon and olive oil, then loosened with pasta water. The method is the standard one.

broccoli-potato-and-cheddar-frittata.note: 10 eggs in a 10-inch skillet, set at the edges on the stove, then 375°F for 14–18 min. Published: 8–12 eggs, 350–375°F, 15–30 min depending on pan. Ours has a center-set/160°F cue to cover the deeper pan.

brown-butter-blondies.note: 1/2 cup browned butter, 1 cup brown sugar and 1 cup flour in an 8-inch pan at 350F for 22-27 min matches published blondies (20-25 min). Soft provenance note: close to Love From the Oven's brown butter blondies, though ours adds a yolk and baking powder.

buffalo-chicken-dip.note: 8 oz cream cheese, 1/2 cup hot sauce, 1/2 cup sour cream and 3 cups chicken with cheddar and blue cheese, baked at 350°F for 20–25 minutes. Published versions use 8 oz cream cheese, 1/2 cup hot sauce and 1/2 cup ranch with 2 cups chicken, at 350°F for 20–25 minutes. Sour cream in place of dressing still works.

buffalo-chicken-wings.note: Baking powder (1 tbsp per 3 lb), 250°F for 30 min, then 425°F for 45–50 min to at least 165°F. buffalo-chicken-wraps.note: Seared chicken tossed in hot sauce and butter, rolled in warmed tortillas with romaine and a creamy dressing: same build as the published wraps. No change.

buttermilk-biscuits-and-sausage-gravy.note: Biscuits: 2 1/2 cups flour, 1 stick butter, 1 cup (plus 1–2 tbsp) buttermilk, 1 tbsp BP plus 1/2 tsp soda, 450°F for 13–16 min. buttermilk-hush-puppies.note: 1 cup cornmeal, 1/2 cup flour, 1 egg and 3/4 cup buttermilk with baking powder and soda matches the published batter (1 cup cornmeal, 1/2 cup flour, 1 egg, about 1 cup buttermilk). Frying rounded tablespoons at 350°F is inside the published 350–365°F, and ours includes a check that the centers are cooked.

butternut-squash-soup.note: Swanson uses a 2–2 1/2 lb squash with 4 cups of broth plus apple, onion and sage, which is the same build. Our 3 lb whole squash (about 2 1/4 lb trimmed) with 4 cups, simmered 20–25 minutes and thinned to taste, is in range.

cabbage-and-kielbasa-skillet.note: Browned kielbasa, then a head of cabbage wilted in butter with onion, finished with cider vinegar and Dijon. This is the same method and flavoring as the published skillets, which cook the cabbage 10–15 minutes. In line.

caesar-salad.note: Mayo-based Caesar dressings with anchovy, garlic, lemon, Dijon, Worcestershire and Parmesan are a standard no-raw-egg approach. Our amounts (1/3 cup mayo, 1/3 cup oil, 4 anchovies) sit next to Hamilton Beach's (1/2 cup mayo, 1/3 cup oil, 3 anchovies). Croutons at 375°F for 10–14 minutes are fine.

cajun-shrimp-and-rice-skillet.note: 1 cup rice to 1 1/2 cups broth plus an undrained 14.5-oz can of tomatoes, simmered covered 18 minutes before the shrimp go in for 5–6 minutes. That sits inside the range of published stovetop versions (2–2.5 cups broth plus tomatoes per cup of rice in Hormel's version, less in others), and the shrimp also go in at the end there.

caprese-salad.note: 3 tomatoes, 8 oz fresh mozzarella, basil, olive oil, salt and optional balsamic: inside published amounts (2-4 tomatoes, 8-12 oz mozzarella for 4).

caramel-flan.note: Condensed + evaporated milk with 4 eggs and 2 yolks in a 9-inch round in a water bath at 350F matches published flans; sources say 50-60 min and ours says 45-55 with a jiggle and knife test, which overlaps and guards against underbaking.

caramelized-french-onion-dip.note: 1 1/2 lb onions caramelized for 35–40 minutes, cooled, then folded into 1 1/2 cups sour cream and 1/3 cup mayonnaise and chilled. Published versions caramelize for 20–60 minutes and use about 1 cup sour cream to 1/4–1/2 cup mayonnaise per two onions.

carrot-cake-with-cream-cheese-frosting.note: 9x13 sheet with 2 1/4 cups flour, 4 eggs, 2 cups sugar, 1 cup oil and 1 lb carrots sits between Joy of Baking (2 1/2 cups flour, 3/4 cup oil plus buttermilk) and Cook's Illustrated (1 1/2 cups oil); 350F for 35-40 min matches both.

cauliflower-cheese.note: The sauce had 1/4 cup flour (about 31 g) to 2 1/2 cups milk, about 53 g per litre. I raised the flour to 1/3 cup (about 71 g/L) and changed nothing else.

chana-masala.note: 2 cans chickpeas, a 14.5 oz can of tomatoes and 1 cup water over well-browned onions, ground coriander and cumin, garam masala at the end; Laura Vitale uses 2 cans, 14 oz tomatoes and 1 1/2 cups water. No change.

cheddar-chive-scones.note: 2 cups flour, 2 1/2 tsp baking powder, 6 tbsp butter, buttermilk and an egg with cheddar and chives, 8 wedges at 400F for 18-22 min, matches published savory scones (2 cups flour, 400F, 8 wedges, 20-24 min).

cheddar-grits-with-fried-eggs.note: 1 cup quick grits to 4 cups water and milk is the package and published ratio. Ours simmers 10–12 min where packages say 5–7, which only makes the grits creamier, and it says to add water if they thicken. Cheese and butter go in off the heat.

cheeseburger-macaroni-skillet.note: One-pot versions cook about 8 oz (2 cups) of elbows covered for 12–15 minutes in 2 1/2–3 cups of liquid. Ours uses 2 1/2 cups of broth, then adds 1/2 cup of milk with the cheese off the heat. That's the low end of the range, but there's a cue to add water and the stirring is frequent.

aligned.note: Liquid cooked with 8 oz elbows: She's Not Cookin 3 cups (2 broth + 1 milk, covered 12–15 min), Together as Family 3 cups (2 broth + 1 milk, 9–11 min), Taste of Home 3 3/4 cups (3 broth + 3/4 milk, 10–15 min); Salt & Lavender's 3 cups of broth for 1 cup of macaroni is an outlier. Median 3 cups and about 12–14 minutes. Ours now cooks the macaroni in 3 cups (our own 2 1/2 broth + 1/2 milk split, so it doesn't copy the 2 + 1 formula), with 2 cups cheddar off the heat. The liquid is no longer at the low edge, so it scores 5.

cheeseburger-soup.note: Works as written: roux-thickened broth and milk with potatoes, cheese added on low. Ours differs in beef (1 lb vs 1/2), cheese (cheddar vs Velveeta), potato weight, method order, mustard and Worcestershire, and has no sour cream.

cheesy-beef-and-bean-tostadas.note: Oil-brushed corn tortillas baked at 400°F for 8–12 minutes with a flip. Sources bake at 400–425°F for 8–14 minutes and also note the shells crisp as they cool. Bean and beef toppings are standard.

cheesy-beef-and-spinach-pasta-bake.note: Beef, tomato and cream cheese sauces with wilted spinach, tossed with underdone pasta and baked 15–25 minutes, are common. Our 28 oz of crushed tomatoes plus cream cheese and pasta water for 12 oz of rotini, at 375°F for 20–25 minutes, fits.

cheesy-chicken-enchiladas.note: Roux-based red sauce (3 tbsp oil and flour, 1/4 cup chili powder, tomato paste, 2 1/2 cups broth) is the standard homemade enchilada sauce; tortillas are warmed so they roll; 12 in a 9x13 at 375°F for 20-25 min with a cooked filling is in range. No change.

cherry-pie.note: 6 cups cherries with 1/4 cup cornstarch and 3/4 cup sugar, plus lemon and almond, matches published fillings. Total bake of 60–70 minutes, starting hot and then lowering the oven, is in line with the 60–70 minute schedules in the sources. All-butter crust ratio (2 1/2 cups flour to 1 cup butter) is standard.

chewy-honey-oat-granola-bars.note: Binder of honey, brown sugar and butter boiled briefly plus peanut butter for ~3 cups of oats and rice cereal matches Real Life Dinner's no-bake bars (1/4 cup each honey, butter, brown sugar, peanut butter for 3 cups); ours has a little more honey, is pressed hard and chilled, so it should hold.

classic-beef-lasagna.note: 9x13 pan, 12 boiled noodles, ricotta with egg and Parmesan, and 1 lb mozzarella, baked at 375°F for 25 minutes under foil plus 25–30 uncovered. Sources bake 45–60 minutes at 375°F with foil first. Ours is in range.

classic-cheesecake.note: 2 lb cream cheese, 1 cup sugar, 4 eggs, sour cream and a little flour in a 9-inch springform at 325F with no water bath matches Kraft's Philadelphia versions (55 min plain, about 70 min with sour cream and flour); our 65-75 min plus oven cool-down is in line.

classic-chicken-pot-pie.note: All-butter single crust (1 1/4 cups flour, 8 tbsp butter), filling thickened with 1/4 cup flour per 2 cups broth and milk, 9-inch deep dish at 400°F. Published single-crust pies bake 35-55 min at 400°F; ours bakes 30-35 min, reasonable because the filling is already cooked and goes in hot. No change.

classic-coleslaw.note: The amount of dressing is in range. ATK dresses a 2 lb head with about 3/4 cup of mayo and sour cream, and Food Network uses about 1 cup for 9 cups of slaw. Ours is 3/4 cup mayo plus 3 tbsp vinegar for 2 lb of cabbage and 2 carrots, chilled 1 hour.

classic-grilled-cheese.note: Cold-pan, medium-low method is right, but 3-4 minutes a side was short: published low-heat versions take about 5-7 min on the first side from a cold pan and 4-5 or more on the second (Cook's Illustrated 5-10 per side). Changed the times to 5-7 and 4-5 minutes and cookMinutes 8 to 11.

classic-grilled-cheeseburgers.note: 6-oz, 3/4-inch patties with a thumb dimple, salted just before cooking, then grilled lid-closed on medium-high for 8–10 minutes total with cheese in the last minute, to 160°F. This matches Weber's method and times.

classic-popovers.note: 3 eggs, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1 1/2 cups flour in a hot 12-cup muffin tin, 425F then 350F, is the standard popover ratio and schedule used by several published versions.

classic-pot-roast-with-carrots-and-potat.note: Seared 3 1/2 lb chuck braised at 325°F in 2 cups broth: 2 hours, then 1–1 1/2 hours more with the vegetables. Sources braise at 275–325°F for 3–4 hours in 2–3 cups broth and add the vegetables for the last 45–90 minutes. Ours is in line.

classic-scones.note: 2 cups flour with 1 tbsp baking powder, 5 tbsp butter, an egg and 1/2 cup milk scales to the BBC-style 350 g flour / 85 g butter / 175 ml milk; 425F for 12-15 min matches the 220C, 10-15 min sources.

classic-waffles.note: 2 cups flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 2 separated eggs, 1 3/4 cups milk and 1/2 cup butter is the classic separated-egg waffle ratio (sources: 2 cups flour, 3–4 tsp BP, 1 1/4–1 3/4 cups milk). The method folds whipped whites in last.

cobb-salad.note: The vinaigrette is in the published range: about 1/4 cup red wine vinegar and a little Dijon to 1/3–1/2 cup oil (ours is 3 tbsp to 1/2 cup). The row layout is classic. Chicken is pounded to 3/4 inch and cooked to 165°F.

coconut-pecan-magic-cookie-bars.note: Same structure as Eagle Brand's bars (graham crust, 14 oz condensed milk, chips, coconut, nuts in a 9x13 at 350F or 325F for glass, ~25 min); ours pre-bakes the crust and uses less chocolate, which is fine.

coconut-shrimp-with-sweet-chili-lime-sau.note: Flour, egg, then coconut and panko, fried at 350°F for 2–3 minutes. Published versions all fry at 350°F for about 1 1/2–3 minutes, and they serve it with a sweet chili dip.

corn-chowder.note: Same structure as published versions: bacon, a light roux, broth, potatoes simmered about 10–20 minutes, then corn and dairy. Our 4 cups of corn and 1 lb of potatoes to about 5 1/2 cups of liquid serves 6, in line with Julie's Eats & Treats. I found no single-source match.

corned-beef-and-cabbage.note: Gentle simmer at about 50 minutes per pound, the same rule the sources give. The vegetables get 22–25 minutes in all (potatoes and carrots 10, then cabbage 12–15), against 25–45 minutes in the sources. Our potatoes are halved small ones and the step ends on 'until tender', so it works.

corned-beef-hash-with-fried-eggs.note: 1 1/2 lb potatoes parboiled 4–5 min, then pressed and crusted in a heavy skillet with 12 oz corned beef. Matches published hash (parboil 3–6 min, 1–1 1/2 lb corned beef, press for a crust).

crab-cakes.note: Binder for 1 lb lump crab (1/3 cup mayo, 1 egg, about 1/2 cup saltine crumbs, Dijon, Worcestershire, Old Bay) and a 30-minute chill sit inside published Maryland-style ranges (1/4-1/2 cup mayo, 2/3-1 cup crackers). Pan-frying 4-5 min a side is standard. No single-source match found.

cream-of-mushroom-soup.note: Hearth & Vine uses 3 cups of broth and 1 cup of cream for 4, and ours uses 3 cups of broth, 3/4 cup of cream and 1/4 cup of flour. Ours uses more mushrooms (1 1/2 lb) and blends them. That's a common restaurant-style approach, though none of the sources I found blend.

creamed-spinach.note: 1 1/2 lb fresh spinach, wilted and squeezed dry, in a 2 tbsp butter / 2 tbsp flour roux with 1 1/2 cups milk and cream matches the steakhouse method (Emeril: 2 lb spinach, blond roux, milk and a splash of cream).

creamy-broccoli-potato-soup.note: Potato-thickened, cream-free versions simmer the potatoes and broccoli in broth until tender, then blend. creamy-chicken-spinach-pasta.note: Checked cream and Parmesan per pound of pasta: published chicken-Alfredo-style pastas use about 1-2 cups cream and 1-1.5 cups Parmesan per lb; ours (1 cup cream, 3/4 cup Parmesan per 12 oz, plus pasta water) is inside that range. Method is standard.

crispy-cornmeal-fried-catfish.note: Buttermilk soak and seasoned cornmeal dredge, fried at 350°F for 4–6 minutes per batch to 145°F. This matches Cook's Country (325–350°F, about 5 minutes) and the other sources.

crispy-roasted-chickpeas.note: Towel-dried canned chickpeas at 400°F for 30-40 min, spices after roasting: matches published versions (400°F, 20-40 min, dry thoroughly, crisp as they cool).

croque-madame.note: 2 tbsp butter / 2 tbsp flour béchamel with 1 1/4 cups milk, sandwiches baked at 425°F then optionally broiled, a fried egg on top. Matches published versions (425°F, 5–10 min plus broil). Ham and Gruyère season it, so no salt is needed.

cuban-beef-picadillo-with-potatoes.note: The potatoes are pan-fried crisp and set aside. The beef browns to 160F, then sofrito, cumin and oregano, a little white wine, and 1 cup tomato sauce with olives and raisins, simmered 10-12 min. Forked Spoon uses 1 cup sauce and 1/4 cup wine. Matches.

cuban-sandwich.note: Pork tenderloin in an orange-lime-garlic-cumin mojo is a published shortcut (Williams-Sonoma, John T. Edge) for the usual shoulder. Roasting at 425°F for 20–25 minutes to 145°F, then a buttered, pressed skillet with ham, Swiss, pickles and yellow mustard, is sound.

dark-chocolate-truffles.note: 2:1 dark chocolate to cream ganache (8 oz to 1/2 cup), chilled about 2 h, scooped and rolled in cocoa, is the standard firm rolling ganache (sources use 1/2-1 cup cream per 8 oz).

deviled-eggs.note: Bring to a boil, then 12 min covered off the heat and an ice bath: the standard method. For 6 eggs the filling (1/4 cup mayo, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tsp vinegar) is inside the published 3–4 tbsp mayo and 1/2–1 tsp mustard and vinegar.

double-chocolate-cookies.note: Ratios (1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup cocoa, 3/4 cup butter, 1 1/4 cups sugars, 2 eggs, 3/4 tsp soda) sit within published double-chocolate cookies. 350°F for 9–11 minutes, pulled while the centers look soft, matches.

dutch-baby-pancake.note: 3 eggs, 2/3 cup milk and 2/3 cup flour in a preheated 10-inch skillet at 425°F for 18–22 min is the common Dutch baby formula (Betty Crocker 425°F/20 min; Palatable Pastime 450°F/18–25). It is shared by several publishers, so no single-source flag.

easy-tomato-soup.note: Checked tomatoes to liquid and simmer: two 28-oz cans with about 2 cups broth matches Six Sisters' ratio; our 15-minute simmer is shorter than the 30-40 min some use, but canned tomatoes are already cooked and the soup is blended, so it works.

egg-and-cheese-english-muffin-sandwiches.note: One egg fried over-hard with cheese melted under a lid, on a toasted buttered muffin, is the standard homemade version. Times and heat are sensible.

egg-salad-sandwiches.note: An 11-minute off-heat stand is inside the published 10–15 minutes. Our 8 eggs to 1/3 cup mayo with Dijon, celery and chives is standard. A Cooklang version shares 8 eggs, 1 rib of celery, 2 tbsp chives and 1 tsp lemon juice. Its mayo, mustard and salt differ, so this isn't a provenance match; egg salads converge on these numbers.

eggplant-parmesan.note: The eggplant is cut in 1/2-inch slices, salted, coated in panko and Parmesan and baked at 425F for 25-30 min (published: 30-35). The layered bake of 25-30 min at 375F matches the published ranges.

falafel-with-tahini-sauce.note: Uses dried chickpeas soaked 12-24 h, never canned. Baking powder 1/2 tsp per cup (published 1/4-3/4) and frying at 350F (published 350-375) are in range. 2 tbsp flour is a little more binder than most use, which does no harm. I reworded the soaking clause only, because it was close to a published sentence.

fattoush.note: Baked sumac pita chips, romaine, tomato, cucumber, radish and herbs in a lemon-sumac dressing (4 tbsp oil to 3 tbsp lemon), tossed just before serving: matches published fattoush.

feijoada.note: 1 lb black beans, quick-soaked, with bacon, 1 1/2 lb pork shoulder and smoked sausage (kielbasa is a substitute La Sirena Clandestina's chef suggests for linguica), simmered 2-2 1/4 h in 7 cups water until creamy. fish-tacos-with-lime-slaw.note: Chili and cumin-rubbed cod seared 3–4 minutes, then 2–3 minutes after turning, served with cabbage slaw and a sour cream lime crema. Published skillet versions use 2–5 minutes per side with the same slaw and crema.

fluffy-pancakes.note: 1 tbsp baking powder per 1 1/2 cups flour (2 tsp per cup) sits inside the published 1 1/3-2 1/3 tsp range; 1/4 cup per pancake over medium is standard. french-dip-sandwiches.note: Quick jus of caramelized onion, beef broth, Worcestershire and soy. Deli beef is only warmed in the jus, then topped with provolone on toasted rolls and melted. Same build and jus seasoning as the sources, including the warning not to cook the beef further.

fresh-strawberry-pie.note: Glaze of blended berries, 3 tbsp cornstarch and 3/4 cup sugar boiled to clear, folded with whole berries in a fully baked 9-inch crust and chilled, matches Eatright's version (3 tbsp cornstarch, 2/3 cup sugar, ~1 3/4 cups liquid).

fried-green-tomatoes.note: Slices about 1/3 inch thick are salted and dried, then breaded in flour, egg-buttermilk and cornmeal, and fried at 350°F for 2–3 minutes a side, all matching published versions (1/4–1/3 inch, 350–375°F). Ours uses 1/4 inch of oil and tells you to top it up; sources often use 1/2–1 inch, but skillet frying in a shallow layer is common and works.

fried-shrimp-po-boys-with-remoulade.note: Shrimp soaked in buttermilk and hot sauce, dredged in seasoned cornmeal and flour, and fried at 350°F in 2 inches of oil, as in the published versions. The mayo-mustard-pickle remoulade and the assembly are standard.

fudgy-brownies.note: 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup sugar, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup flour in an 8-inch pan matches the Hershey's-style one-bowl formula; ours adds 4 oz dark chocolate with less cocoa. 350F for 25-30 min with a moist-crumb test is in the 20-30 min range sources give.

gado-gado.note: 1 lb potatoes and 4 eggs hard-boiled 10 min (as Vice), with blanched green beans, cabbage and sprouts and fried tofu. The warm peanut sauce of peanut butter, water, soy, sugar and lime is thinned to pour. Matches.

garlic-bread.note: 1/2 cup butter per 1 lb loaf, split lengthwise and baked at 400°F for 10–12 min, is the common formula (sources: 400°F, 8–15 min).

garlic-butter-shrimp.note: 1 lb shrimp seared about 1-2 min per side, then tossed in garlic butter and lemon: matches published versions (about 2 min per side; garlic 30-60 s).

garlic-chicken-spinach-skillet.note: Compared bite-size chicken cook time and method: published versions sear 1-inch breast pieces about 6-8 minutes to 165°F, then add garlic briefly; ours (3 + 3-4 min, garlic last, spinach wilted in) matches.

garlic-green-beans.note: Covered skillet steam with a little water 4-5 minutes, uncover to evaporate, then butter and garlic 1-2 minutes: same method and timing as published versions.

garlic-herb-pork-tenderloin.note: Seared, then roasted at 425°F for 10–15 minutes to 145°F. Published versions use 425°F for 15–20 minutes, or a sear and then 15–18 minutes, both to 145°F.

garlic-lemon-grilled-shrimp-skewers.note: Short lemon-garlic marinade (15–30 minutes), skewered twice so the shrimp lie flat, and grilled on medium-high for 2–3 minutes a side to opaque. This matches published marinade limits (15 minutes to 2 hours) and grill times.

garlic-parmesan-knots.note: 3 cups flour, 1 cup water, a packet of yeast and olive oil for 16 knots at 400F for 15-18 min matches published garlic knots (3 cups flour, 16-18 knots, 375-400F), finished in garlic butter and Parmesan.

general-tsos-chicken.note: Thigh pieces in an egg and soy marinade, coated in cornstarch and flour, fried at 350F in 2 inches of oil, as in Boston.com. The sauce is broth, soy, vinegar, sugar and hoisin thickened with 1 tbsp cornstarch, with dried chilies. Cooked to 165F.

german-potato-salad.note: Waxy potatoes boiled whole, sliced warm and dressed with hot bacon fat, onion, cider vinegar, broth, sugar and Dijon: classic method. 1/3 cup vinegar + 1/3 cup broth + 2 tbsp sugar for 2 1/2 lb is within published amounts (2 tbsp-1/2 cup vinegar, 1/2 cup broth, 2 tbsp sugar per 2 lb).

gingerbread-cookies.note: Cut-out dough ratios, 1/4-inch thickness and 350°F for 8–10 minutes all match published versions. kuku-sabzi.note: 8 eggs to about 6 cups of packed herbs and green onion (one published version uses 8 eggs to 5 cups), walnuts, a little baking powder. It's set on the stovetop, then baked at 350F for 20-25 min until firm (published: 20-35 min at 350-375F).

aligned.changed: baking powder 1/2 → 1 tsp; oven 350°F (175°C) → 375°F (190°C)
aligned.note: Baking powder: 1 tsp in Food Network, Delicious Crescent, James Beard and eggs.ca (6–8 eggs), 1 1/2 tsp in Rogers Gardens and Experience Life: typical 1 tsp, ours 1/2 was the low edge. Oven: 375F in Delicious Crescent, Rogers Gardens, eggs.ca and Experience Life (350F only in CTV and one 350–375 version), so 375F. Bake time already typical: 20–25 min after the 4–5 min stovetop start (oven-only versions bake 20–35). Kept: 8 eggs to about 6 cups packed herbs and green onion (The Mediterranean Dish uses 8 eggs to 5 cups), 1 1/4 tsp salt for 8 eggs (eggs.ca and Experience Life about 1 1/2 tsp kosher or sea salt for 8), 1 tbsp flour (Delicious Crescent 1 tbsp), 10-inch skillet. Scores 5.

kung-pao-chicken.note: Cornstarch-soy velveted thighs, chilies bloomed in oil, small soy-vinegar-sugar sauce with cornstarch, peanuts at the end; 8-12 chilies sits in the usual 8-10 range. No change.

lamb-gyros-with-tzatziki.note: 1 1/2 lb kneaded ground lamb pressed into a 9x5 loaf pan and baked at 350°F for 40–45 minutes to 160°F. Published loaf versions use 325–350°F for 35–70 minutes depending on size, usually with 2 lb. Ours is a thinner loaf (under an inch deep), so the shorter time with a thermometer check works.

aligned.changed: loaf bake 40–45 → 45–50 minutes (still 350°F, 9x5 pan, to 160°F); cookMinutes 60 → 65
aligned.note: Loaf versions bake 2 lb of meat in a 9x5 pan at 350°F for 60 (Kitchen Dreaming), 50–60 (The Modern Proper) and about 60 minutes (Foreign Fork). A Spicy Perspective is the outlier at 400°F for 30–35. The median is 350°F (ours already) and about 55–60 minutes for 2 lb. Scaled to our 1 1/2 lb (three-quarters the depth in the same pan), that is about 45–50 minutes, so the time moved up from the short end. Salt (1 tsp per lb) is inside the published 0.25–1 tsp per lb. The house rule keeps 160°F for ground meat (the sources say 165°F). Scores 5.

lemon-bars.note: 9x13 crust of 2 cups flour and 1 cup butter is the standard; filling of 5 eggs, 1 3/4 cups sugar, 1/3 cup flour and 3/4 cup lemon juice is inside the 4-6 eggs and 1/3-1 cup juice range. Par-baked crust and ~20 min filling bake match.

lemon-drizzle-cake.note: A 3-egg version of the 4-egg equal-weights loaf (225 g each butter, sugar, flour); 350F for 45-50 min in a 9x5 and a juice-and-sugar drizzle on the hot cake match BBC Good Food-style recipes.

lemon-garlic-baked-cod.note: 1-inch cod at 400°F for 12–15 minutes under a buttered panko topping. Published versions use 400°F for 11–20 minutes depending on thickness, to 145°F.

lemon-garlic-roasted-potatoes.note: 425°F for about 40 minutes for 1 1/2-inch Yukon chunks sits inside the published 30-55 minute range; adding the garlic only for the last 5 minutes and lemon off the heat avoids burnt garlic.

lemon-herb-chicken-thighs-with-roasted-p.note: Bone-in thighs with 1 1/2-inch potato chunks at 425°F for 40-45 min matches published sheet-pan versions (30-50 min at 425°F, checked at 165°F). No change.

lemon-meringue-pie.note: Filling of 1 1/2 cups water, 1/3 cup cornstarch, 4 yolks, 1/2 cup lemon juice and 1 1/4 cups sugar, re-boiled after tempering, matches published pies; 4-white meringue with 1/2 cup sugar spread on hot filling and baked at 350F is standard.

lemon-poppy-seed-muffins.note: 2 cups flour with 2 tsp baking powder and 1/2 tsp soda, 2 eggs, sour cream and melted butter for 12 muffins is inside the published range. 375°F for 18–22 minutes is a normal muffin bake. The glaze of powdered sugar and lemon juice is standard.

lentil-shepherds-pie.note: 1 1/2 cups brown or green lentils simmer in 4 cups broth for 30-35 min, reducing to a gravy (Hey Nutrition Lady uses 1 1/2 cups to 3 cups), under 3 lb of mash baked at 400F for 25 min (published 15-20 plus broil). In range.

loaded-nachos-with-black-beans.note: Two layers of chips, beans and cheese at 400°F for 8–10 min, with fresh toppings added after baking. Matches published sheet-pan nachos (400–425°F, 5–10 min).

loco-moco.note: 6-oz patties cooked to 160°F, then a pan gravy of about 3 tbsp fat, 2 tbsp flour and 1 1/2 cups beef broth with soy and Worcestershire, over rice with a fried egg. Matches published loco moco.

macaroni-salad.note: 8 oz of macaroni to 1 cup of mayo with 2 tbsp cider vinegar is the standard ratio (Betty Crocker-derived and Farm and Dairy versions). Cooking the pasta soft, rinsing it and holding back some dressing are sound. I found no single-source match.

mapo-tofu.note: Salted-water-blanched tofu, pork, 2 1/2 tbsp doubanjiang, 1 cup broth, 1 tbsp cornstarch slurry added in stages, ground toasted Sichuan peppercorn; published versions use 1 lb tofu, 1/2-1 cup stock, 2-3 tbsp doubanjiang, 1 tbsp cornstarch. No change.

marshmallow-crispy-rice-treats.note: Ours uses 6 tbsp butter, 16 oz marshmallows and 8 cups cereal in a 9x13. Published brown-butter versions use 6 tbsp/16 oz/7 cups and 8 tbsp/20 oz/9 cups, so ours falls between them. Holding back some marshmallows matches published versions.

mashed-sweet-potatoes.note: Boil 2-inch chunks 12-15 min, brown the butter, add milk and maple, mash: same method as published brown-butter versions. 4 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp maple for 3 lb is leaner than some (5-6 tbsp, 1/4 cup) but within taste range.

meatball-subs.note: Published versions bake 1 lb beef meatballs at 400°F for 15–30 minutes, simmer them in marinara and melt mozzarella over the filled rolls. Ours bakes 18–20 minutes to 160°F.

mediterranean-chickpea-buddha-bowls.note: Quinoa at 1 cup to 1 3/4 cups water (simmer 15, rest 5), the standard ratio. Chickpeas and sweet potato roasted at 425°F for 25–30 minutes, and lemon tahini thinned with water. All match published versions.

mexican-street-corn.note: Broil oiled ears 12-16 min, turning, then mayo-sour cream-lime crema, cotija and chili powder: same timing and build as Tasting Table (broil 12-16 min) and others.

molasses-crinkle-cookies.note: 2 1/4 cups flour, 2 tsp soda, 3/4 cup fat, ~1 cup sugar, 1 egg and 1/4-1/3 cup molasses is the classic molasses crinkle formula; chilled dough, sugar roll and 350F for 10-12 min are standard (sources 375F, ~10 min).

molten-chocolate-lava-cakes.note: 4 oz chocolate, 1 stick butter, 2 eggs + 2 yolks for 4 ramekins matches Baker's (425F, 13-14 min) and the widely reprinted Jean-Georges formula; 425F for 12-14 min is inside the 11-14 min range at 425F. Soft provenance note: chocolate/butter/egg/sugar amounts equal Jean-Georges' (ours 2 tbsp flour vs 2 tsp, different oven).

aligned.changed: flour 2 tbsp -> 3 tbsp
aligned.note: Per 4 cakes: chocolate 4 oz (Baker's, Carlsbad, Jean-Georges, Crate & Barrel; Once Upon a Chef scaled; Sally's 6), butter 1 stick, 2 eggs + 2 yolks and about 50-60 g sugar are all typical and ours already matched. Flour runs 2 tsp (Jean-Georges), 1 tbsp (Crate & Barrel), 2 tbsp (Once Upon a Chef scaled), 1/4 cup (Sally's), 6 tbsp (Baker's) and 6 1/3 tbsp (Carlsbad): median 3 tbsp, so ours moved from 2 to 3. 425F is the most common oven (Baker's, Carlsbad, Sally's; 450F in Jean-Georges, Once Upon a Chef, Crate & Barrel), and 12-14 min matches the 425F versions (13-14, 11-13). The wobbling-center cue stays. With 3 tbsp flour and 425F for 12-14 min it no longer shares Jean-Georges' formula (2 tsp flour, 450F for 6-7 min), which settles the soft provenance note. Score 5.

mongolian-beef.note: Cornstarch-coated flank shallow-fried in batches, then tossed in 1/2 cup soy, 1/3 cup brown sugar and 1/3 cup water. Sources use a soy-to-sugar ratio from 2:1 to 1:1.5, with the cornstarch coating thickening the sauce. Ours sits inside that range on the less sweet side. Method matches.

Cornstarch coating per lb: 1/2 cup dredge (Woks of Life), 1/3 cup (Cooking Guy), 1/4 cup (Fox Valley), 2 tbsp (Chili Pepper Madness, Modern Proper). The median is 1/4 cup per lb, so 6 tbsp for 1 1/2 lb; ours had 2 2/3 tbsp per lb. As in Fox Valley Foodie and The Cooking Guy, which use no slurry, the coating thickens the sauce when the beef goes back in. Brown sugar 1/3 cup (3.6 tbsp per lb; median 4: 2, 3, 4, 8, 12) and soy 1/2 cup (5.3 tbsp per lb; total soy in the sources 4.3–11, median about 6) already sit at the typical values and stay. The soy-to-sugar ratio of 1.5:1 is within the 0.7–2.5 range. The audit's existing 'water per cup of rice' flag now reads 0.5 instead of 0.22: the water is for the sauce, and the rice is cooked as the package directs. The pre-existing 'flank_steak with no internal temperature' flag is unchanged; this is a thin-strip stir-fry, not a steak cooked to doneness.

moussaka.note: Roasted eggplant (as Ruhlman does), potato base, spiced beef in tomato and wine, and a thick béchamel (6 tbsp butter, 1/2 cup flour, 3 cups milk, 2 yolks). It bakes at 350°F for 45–50 minutes in a 9x13 and rests 20. Sources bake 35–60 minutes at 350°F. In line.

muhammara.note: 1 cup toasted walnuts and 1/2 cup bread crumbs to a 16-oz jar of roasted peppers, with 2 tbsp pomegranate molasses, lemon and 3 tbsp oil. Published versions use 3/4–1 1/3 cups walnuts, 1/4–3/4 cup crumbs and 2 tsp–3 tbsp molasses per 8–15 oz peppers.

mujadara.note: Lentils par-boiled, onions fried deep brown in olive oil, rice cooked with the lentils in 1 3/4 cups water and spices; ATK also par-cooks lentils and uses equal lentils and rice. The audit's liquid flag counts the lentil boiling water. No change.

mushroom-and-black-bean-tacos.note: Mushrooms browned without stirring, chipotle, beans, a quick pico and charred corn tortillas. A simple method that matches the published chipotle mushroom and bean tacos.

mussels-in-white-wine-and-garlic.note: 4 lb mussels steamed covered for 4–6 minutes in 1 cup wine with shallots, garlic and butter. Published versions use 150–250 ml wine per 2 kg (MSC, Delicious) up to about 3/4 cup per kg, and 3–8 minutes covered. Discarding open or uncooked mussels is covered.

nicoise-salad.note: Vinaigrette of 3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 2 tsp Dijon and 1/2 cup oil (about 1:2.7). Williams-Sonoma uses 3 tbsp vinegar to 10 tbsp oil. Eggs cook 8–10 minutes, beans 3–4 minutes and potatoes until tender, as in published versions.

no-bake-peanut-butter-bars.note: Base of 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup peanut butter, 1 1/2 cups crumbs and 2 cups powdered sugar sits inside the published range (1/2–1 cup butter, 1–2 cups crumbs, 1–2 cups sugar per cup of peanut butter). Topping is chips plus a little peanut butter, as in the sources.

oat-flapjacks.note: 125 g butter, ~100 g brown sugar, 110 g golden syrup and 250 g oats in an 8-inch (20 cm) tin at 350F (180C) for 20-25 min matches traditional flapjacks (125/90/90/250 g, 180C, 15-30 min).

omurice.note: Ketchup chicken rice (1 cup rice per plate) with a soft 2-egg omelette draped over: the standard build. Published omelettes use 1–3 eggs per plate, and frying the ketchup before adding the rice is the usual step.

aligned.changed: chicken thighs 8 → 5 oz; ketchup total 1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp → 5 tbsp (in the rice 1/4 cup → 3 tbsp; 2 tbsp on top unchanged)

Ketchup cooked into the rice: 2 1/2, 1/2, 1 1/2, 1 and 4 tbsp → median 1 1/2 → 3 tbsp for 2. Kept: 1 cup cooked rice per plate (median 1), 2 eggs per omelette (1–2), 1 tsp butter per omelette, 1/3 cup peas (published 1 tbsp to 1/2 cup). Our chicken and ketchup were at the top of the range and now sit at the median, so it scores 5.

one-pot-chicken-and-orzo-with-spinach.note: 1 1/2 cups orzo to 3 1/2 cups broth (about 2 1/3 to 1), covered 10–12 minutes with browned thigh pieces. The BYU one-pot version uses 2 1/4 cups broth per cup of orzo. In line.

one-pot-chili-mac-with-cheddar.note: Same build and timing as published one-pot chili macs: 1 lb beef, broth, diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, kidney beans and 8 oz of elbows covered 12–15 minutes, cheese melted on top.

oven-baked-bbq-ribs.note: Baby backs covered at 275°F for 2 1/2–3 hours, then sauced at high heat. Published versions use 2 1/2–3 1/2 hours covered, then sauce and broil or bake hot. Doneness cue (meat pulled back from the bones) matches.

oven-baked-caramel-popcorn.note: This caramel (1/2 cup butter, 1 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup corn syrup) coats 10-12 cups of popcorn in Allrecipes (halved), Sally's and Presto, but ours popped 1/2 cup kernels (~15 cups), leaving it thinly coated. Cut kernels to 1/3 cup and the stated yield to about 10 cups. Provenance: caramel amounts and method (4-min boil, soda, 250F for 1 h stirring every 15 min) equal half the Allrecipes 'Caramel Popcorn'.

rework.matched: Allrecipes' Caramel Popcorn, halved (caramel amounts and method)
rework.changed: corn syrup 1/4 cup -> 3 tbsp plus 1 tbsp molasses; salt 3/4 -> 1 tsp (half-Allrecipes 1/2 tsp); caramel boil 4 -> 5 min; oven 250F -> 225F; stirring every 15 -> every 20 min, with a crunch test and 10 more minutes if it chews; tagline. Butter, brown sugar, soda, vanilla and 1/3 cup kernels (about 10 cups) unchanged.
rework.note: Every published baked caramel corn keeps the 1 cup brown sugar : 1/2 cup butter : 1/4 cup liquid sweetener caramel (Allrecipes, Presto, Almanac, Taste of Home, KA's Carol's Caramel Corn), so the brief's 'choices inside the range' apply: liquid sweetener partly molasses as in KA's (which uses 2 tbsp), salt 1/2-1 tsp per cup sugar, boil 4-5 min (Presto, Almanac, KA 5), oven 200-250F (KA, Almanac, Sally's 200F; Allrecipes, Presto 250F), stirring every 15-20 min (Sally's 20), 10-15 cups popcorn per cup of sugar. 225F for an hour sits between those. It doesn't track KA's either (15 cups popcorn, 2 tbsp molasses, salted butter, 200F, no vanilla). A softer score than 5 only because the base caramel is universal.

aligned.note: Popcorn per cup of brown sugar: 10 (Allrecipes/Sweet Pea's), about 10 1/2 counting pretzels (Taste of Home), 12 (Presto), 15 (Almanac), 15 from 9 tbsp kernels (King Arthur's Carol's), 16 (Foodie with Family): median about 13, so ours (10) sat at the heavily coated edge. The change moves it away from the Allrecipes recipe it was reworked from. The caramel (1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup butter, 1/4 cup liquid sweetener), the 5-minute boil, 1/2 tsp soda, 225F (between the 200F and 250F groups) and 1 hour are typical. Salt stays at 1 tsp per cup of sugar, about twice the published 1/4-1/2 tsp, because the rework raised it to move away from Allrecipes' 1/2 tsp and the brief forbids moving back. Stirring every 20 min (Sally's) is kept for the same reason (Allrecipes stirs every 15). Still a 4 only because of that salt edge.

overnight-cinnamon-french-toast-bake.note: 1 lb challah, 8 eggs and 3 cups milk and cream in a 9x13, soaked overnight, streusel on top, 350°F for 45–55 min. Matches published versions (8 eggs, 2 1/2–3 cups dairy, 45–55 min).

overnight-oats.note: 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup milk, 1/4 cup Greek yogurt is the standard 1:1:1/2 ratio; 6+ hours chilled is in line (4 hours to overnight).

oyakodon.note: Uses the standard 4:1:1 broth, soy and mirin donburi base, with onion, thighs simmered to 165F and egg added in two pours, then set off the heat. PROVENANCE (mild): the sauce and chicken amounts are Just One Cookbook's 2-serving card doubled (1 cup liquid, 1/4 cup soy, 1/4 cup mirin, 20 oz thighs), with chicken broth for dashi and 1 tbsp sugar. That ratio is the textbook one, though.

pad-kra-pao.note: The seasoning was too light: 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy and 2 tsp fish sauce for 1 1/2 lb chicken is about 60% of the lowest published salt level. Published versions give about 1 tbsp fish sauce per lb (SJSU, Woks of Life, Tastemade, Observatory) and about 2 tbsp oyster sauce per lb. I raised oyster sauce to 3 tbsp and fish sauce to 1 1/2 tbsp, which lands at the low end of the range. The method is unchanged.

aligned.note: Per lb of chicken, the published sauces give: fish sauce about 1 tbsp (Woks of Life 1, Hungry in Thailand 1, SJSU 1; Pickled Plum and Mediterrasian 2 1/2–3; RecipeTin none), soy (light, golden mountain, dark) about 2 tbsp (WoL 2, HiT 2 1/2, SJSU 2, Pickled Plum 2, RecipeTin 1 1/3), oyster sauce about 1–1 1/2 tbsp where used (SJSU 2/3, RecipeTin 1 1/3, HiT 2, Mediterrasian 4), sugar about 1 1/2 tsp, water or stock about 1/4 cup. For our 1 1/2 lb: fish sauce 1 1/2 tbsp and sugar 2 tsp already typical; soy was 1/3 of typical (1 → 3 tbsp), oyster sauce above it (3 → 2 tbsp), water short (3 tbsp → 1/3 cup). Total salty seasoning is now about 4 1/3 tbsp per lb, the median of the six sources (2 2/3–6 2/3). Not equal to any one source. Scores 5.

palak-paneer.note: Spinach blanched 1 min and shocked in ice water, puréed, cooked into an onion-tomato-spice base and finished with cream and paneer; published methods are the same (1-2 min blanch). No change.

pan-seared-salmon-with-lemon-butter-spin.note: Skin-on fillets cooked mostly skin-side down for 4–5 minutes, then 1–3 minutes after flipping, to 145°F. Published crispy-skin methods use about 4–5 minutes on the skin and a short finish on the flesh.

panzanella.note: 8 oz toasted bread to 2 lb salted, drained tomatoes, with a dressing built on the drained juice. That is the widely used salt-and-drain method (Kenji López-Alt's Food Lab version uses 3/4 lb bread to 2 1/2 lb tomatoes). Ours has different amounts (oil, vinegar, no shallot or Dijon, adds cucumber and soaked onion), so it is not a copy.

pasta-aglio-e-olio.note: 1/3 cup oil and 6 sliced cloves per 12 oz spaghetti, garlic started cold and kept pale, emulsified with pasta water: matches James Beard (1/3 cup oil per lb) and others (100 ml oil, 8 cloves per 400 g).

pasta-e-fagioli.note: Pancetta soffritto, 2 cans cannellini with some mashed back in, 6 cups broth plus tomatoes, and 1 cup ditalini cooked in the soup. ATK cooks 1 cup ditalini in the soup, and Cooking with Nonna uses 2 cans of beans with 6 cups broth and mashes some. In line.

pasta-primavera.note: 12 oz pasta for 4, with the broccoli and peas cooked in the pasta pot and a butter, lemon and Parmesan sauce brought together with pasta water. The U-Michigan version builds it the same way.

patatas-bravas.note: The potatoes are par-boiled 5-7 min (published: 5 min), steam-dried, then shallow-fried in 1/2 inch of oil at 350F, turning, for 8-10 min. Served with a smoked-paprika tomato sauce and garlic mayonnaise. Sound.

patty-melts-on-rye.note: Same as diner-style published versions: deeply caramelized onions (15–30 minutes), thin patties (1/4–1/3 inch), Swiss, and buttered rye griddled over medium-low. Our 5 oz of beef per sandwich is in line with Whitney Bond's 1 1/2 lb for 4.

peach-cobbler.note: 3 lb peaches with 3 tbsp cornstarch, fruit baked first, then a 1 1/2 cup flour / 2 tsp baking powder biscuit topping at 375F matches published biscuit-topped cobblers (one uses the same 3 lb and 1 1/2 cups flour, with cream).

peanut-butter-banana-toast.note: Assembly recipe; peanut butter (about 1-1 1/2 tbsp per slice), banana, optional honey and cinnamon match published versions.

peanut-butter-blossom-cookies.note: Works as written. Provenance: matches Pillsbury's 1957 Bake-Off 'Peanut Blossoms' quantity for quantity (1 3/4 cups flour, 1/2 cup each sugar and brown sugar, 1 tsp soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 cup fat, 1/2 cup peanut butter, 2 tbsp milk, 1 tsp vanilla, 1 egg, 375F); ours swaps butter for the shortening.

rework.matched: Pillsbury's 1957 Bake-Off Peanut Blossoms (1 3/4 c flour, 1/2 c each sugar, 1 tsp soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 c PB, 2 tbsp milk, 375°F)

peanut-butter-cookies.note: Butter, egg, sugar and soda match the classics (1/2 cup butter, 1 egg, ~3/4 tsp soda). Less dough, so 36 cookies of the same size. Doesn't equal National Peanut Board's (1 3/4 cups flour, 1/2 cup peanut butter). Scores 5.

pecan-pie.note: 3 eggs, 3/4 cup each corn syrup and brown sugar, 4 tbsp butter and 2 cups pecans is between Priester's (1/2 cup each) and the 1-cup classics; 350F for 50-60 min with a slight center wobble is in range.

penne-alla-vodka.note: A 28-oz can of tomatoes, 1/3 cup vodka cooked off, 3/4 cup cream and 1 lb penne. Published versions use 1/3-1 cup vodka and 1/2-1 cup cream.

pepper-steak-with-rice.note: Thin sirloin marinated briefly in soy and cornstarch, seared in batches, then peppers and onion, with a broth-soy sauce thickened with cornstarch and boiled 1 minute. This is the standard Chinese-American method in the sources.

peri-peri-chicken.note: Blended chili, roasted red pepper, garlic, lemon, vinegar and smoked paprika marinade, 2 h to overnight, bone-in pieces roasted at 425°F for 35-45 min; published versions roast at 400-430°F to 165°F. No change.

philly-cheesesteak.note: Same technique as published versions: partly freeze the ribeye about 30 minutes, shave it thin, cook it fast over high heat, and use 2 slices of provolone per roll. Our 6 oz of beef per roll is in line with them (several use 1–1 1/2 lb for 4 rolls).

pico-de-gallo.note: 1 lb Romas, white onion, 1–2 jalapeños, cilantro, 2 tbsp lime and 1/2 tsp salt, rested 10–15 min: inside the published ranges (Baked Bree: 1 lb tomatoes, 3 tbsp lime, 1/2 tsp salt).

pineapple-upside-down-cake.note: 9-inch round, 1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup butter, 3/4 cup sugar, 2 eggs and pineapple juice at 350F matches published from-scratch cakes; butter and brown sugar topping and a 10-minute rest before flipping are standard.

porcupine-meatballs-in-tomato-sauce.note: Raw long-grain rice in beef meatballs, simmered covered in tomato sauce with water and brown sugar for 45–60 minutes, matches Taste of Home and African Bites. Our rice is a bit lower (1/2 cup per 1 1/2 lb against 1/2 cup per lb), which means fewer quills but no cooking risk. Cooked to 160°F.

steak-tacos-with-pico-de-gallo.note: Flank marinated in lime 30 minutes to 8 hours, then seared in very hot cast iron 4–5 minutes a side to 130°F. Sources give the same marinade window and 4–5 minutes a side. Pico is standard, and the USDA sentence is present.

swiss-steak-with-tomatoes-and-peppers.note: Alton Brown braises floured, pounded, browned steaks with tomatoes covered at 325°F for 1 1/2–2 hours, and ATK braises blade steaks about 2 hours at 300°F. Our 1 3/4–2 hours at 325°F, with a fork-tender cue, is in range.

tex-mex-migas.note: 8 eggs and 6 corn tortillas fried in strips for 4 servings matches ATK and NPR (8 eggs, 6 tortillas, 4 servings). Ours uses tomato and more Jack where ATK uses bell pepper, so the formula is not ATK's.

thai-mango-sticky-rice.note: 1 1/2 cups glutinous rice to one can of coconut milk with ~1/2 cup sugar is the common pattern (1-1 1/2 cups rice per can); soak 4 h, steam 20-25 min, soak in sweet coconut milk, cornstarch-thickened salty topping all match. tom-kha-gai.note: Two cans of coconut milk to 2 cups broth, with lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves steeped first, 3 tbsp fish sauce, and lime juice added off the heat. Published versions use 1–2 cans per 1–2 cups stock and 1–3 tbsp each of fish sauce and lime, also off the heat.

tomato-bruschetta.note: 1 1/2 lb Romas with basil, garlic, olive oil and a little balsamic on baguette toasted at 400°F and rubbed with garlic matches published versions (400°F, 4–8 min, garlic rub).

tomato-egg-and-cheddar-breakfast-quesadi.note: Soft-scrambled eggs, seeded tomato and cheddar in folded flour tortillas, crisped 2–3 min per side over medium. Matches published breakfast quesadillas.

aligned.note: Flour per cup of milk: Tesco 2, Everyday Elizabeth 2, BBC Good Food 2.5, Food a Fact of Life 3, BHF 3 (Cooked by Julie 1). The median is 2 tbsp; ours had 1, the thin edge. Butter is about 1.1 tbsp per cup (Tesco 1.1, BBC 1.4, Everyday Elizabeth 1), so our 3 tbsp for 3 cups was already typical. Milk per pasta has a median of about 1.9 ml/g (Tesco 1.7, Everyday Elizabeth 2.1, BHF 2.2, BBC and FaFoL 1.0), so our 3 cups per 12 oz (2.1) is kept. Cheddar per cup of milk in the full-fat versions: Everyday Elizabeth 0.25, Tesco 0.4, FaFoL 0.6, BBC 0.9 cups, about 0.5 in the middle, so 1 1/2 cups for 3 cups milk (BHF's reduced-fat 0.2 left out). The 375°F/190°C oven (BBC 180°C, FaFoL 200°C, Everyday Elizabeth 375°F) is kept. Bake time: BBC 15–20, FaFoL 20, Everyday Elizabeth 15–20, so 15–20. Scores 5.

tuscan-chicken-with-sun-dried-tomatoes.note: Cutlets seared 4–5 minutes a side to 165°F, then a sauce of 3/4 cup reduced broth, 1 cup cream and 1/2 cup Parmesan with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach. Sources use 1/3–1 cup broth, 1–1 1/2 cups cream and 1/2 cup Parmesan. In line.

twice-baked-potatoes-with-spinach-and-ch.note: The first bake matches The Kitchn (425°F, 50–60 minutes). The second bake (15–20 minutes) matches eMeals and Williams-Sonoma (about 20 minutes at 400°F). The spinach, cream cheese and cheddar filling is in line with eMeals.

vanilla-cupcakes-with-buttercream.note: 1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup butter, 3/4 cup sugar, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup milk for 12 at 350F for 18-20 min matches published dozen-cupcake recipes; buttercream of 1 cup butter to 3 1/2 cups powdered sugar is standard.

vanilla-panna-cotta.note: One envelope of gelatin for 2 3/4 cups cream and milk is about 0.8 tsp per cup. Published versions use 0.7–0.75 tsp per cup (ATK: 2 3/4 tsp for 4 cups; Mr. Food: 1 envelope for 3 cups), so ours sets slightly firmer, which suits turning it out. Bloom, dissolve off the heat and a 6-hour chill match the sources.

vegetable-fried-rice.note: 3 cups chilled cooked rice, 2 eggs and 2 1/2 tbsp soy sauce sit inside the published range (2-3 tbsp soy per 3 cups rice; eggs scrambled first and returned). Method sound.

vegetable-lasagna-with-spinach-and-ricot.note: Nine par-boiled noodles in a 9x13 with 15 oz ricotta plus an egg, 48 oz marinara and 1 lb mozzarella, at 375F covered then uncovered. The published bakes run 20+10 to 45+5 min; ours is 25 + 20-25. The vegetables are cooked dry first.

vegetable-lo-mein.note: The sauce is 3 tbsp soy and 2 tbsp hoisin, with sesame oil, for 8 oz dried or 1 lb fresh noodles. That is the common ratio (iHeartVegetables and ATK use 3:2 too), and the stir-fry order is sound.

vegetable-pakoras.note: Salted onion, potato and spinach bound with about 1 1/4 cups besan and only enough water (1/3–1/2 cup) to make a thick coating, then fried at 350°F. This matches sources (about 125 g besan to 150 ml water, oil at 350–375°F).

vegetable-tempura-with-soy-ginger-dippin.note: Published batters use about equal volumes of egg plus ice water and flour (1 egg plus 200–240 ml water per cup of flour). Ours had only 3/4 cup water for 1 1/8 cups flour and cornstarch, which gives a heavier coat. I raised the batter water to 1 cup (total water 1 1/4 cups; the sauce keeps its 1/4 cup). Frying at 350°F is inside the published 340–360°F.

aligned.changed: none to the numbers; the sweet potato now has a doneness cue (a skewer slides through it easily)
aligned.note: Batter per cup of flour: Just One Cookbook 1 egg + 200 ml ice water; RecipeTin Japan egg + 200 ml water, matched by an equal volume of flour; Wikibooks, Carmy and Feedmebetter 1 egg + 1 cup ice water. The median is 1 egg and about 1 cup water per cup of flour, which is ours since the earlier fix (1 egg, 1 cup water, 1 cup flour plus 2 tbsp cornstarch). Frying temperature: RecipeTin Japan 335°F for vegetables, Carmy 340, Wikibooks 340-350, Just One Cookbook 350, Martha Stewart (PBS) 350, Feedmebetter 350, MasterClass 360; median 350 (ours 350). About 2-3 minutes a piece matches Martha Stewart (about 3) and Carmy (3-4 for thicker pieces). Nothing sits at an edge, so no number moved. The remaining risk was a sweet potato round left raw in the center, so it now has its own doneness cue. Scores 5.

veggie-egg-muffins.note: 10 eggs plus 1/3 cup milk over 12 cups at 350°F for 20–22 min matches published egg cups (8–10 eggs, 350°F, 14–22 min). Precooking the vegetables avoids watery cups.

victoria-sponge.note: Equal weights of butter, sugar and flour with 4 eggs in two 8-inch (20 cm) pans at 350F, plus jam and cream, is the standard Victoria sponge; 20-25 min with a spring-back test fits the ~25 min sources give.

vietnamese-lemongrass-chicken.note: Lemongrass-shallot-garlic-fish sauce-brown sugar marinade on boneless thighs, pan-seared over medium to 165°F, nuoc cham of sugar dissolved in water with lime, fish sauce, garlic and chili; jasmine rice 1 1/2 cups to 2 cups water. No change.

waldorf-salad.note: A mayo and Greek yogurt dressing with lemon and honey over apples, celery, grapes and toasted walnuts is the published modern version. Our proportions are a little more generously dressed than Love and Lemons'.

wedge-salad-with-blue-cheese-dressing.note: Dressing of mayonnaise, sour cream and buttermilk with 4 oz blue cheese, part mashed and part in chunks. ATK and Wendy Polisi use the same three bases in similar proportions. Wedge assembly is standard.

weeknight-coq-au-vin.note: Bacon, browned bone-in thighs, mushrooms and pearl onions, flour and tomato paste, 2 cups wine plus 1 cup broth, 35 min covered then reduced. Weeknight versions braise about 30 min with 1-2 cups wine. No change.

aligned.note: Weeknight versions with browned thighs braise about 30 min covered (Food Network Kitchen 30, An Edible Mosaic 30, Cooks on Main 20-40, Suburban Soapbox 30-35). Ours was 35, past the typical value. Wine per 8 thighs runs from 1 cup (Food Network, reduced) to 2 cups (Cooks on Main, Suburban Soapbox, Good Sam scaled up), median about 1 3/4-2, with about 1 cup broth. Ours (2 cups wine, 1 cup broth, 2 tbsp flour) already sits there and did not move. The 165°F doneness and the 5-8 min reduction are unchanged. Scores 5.

western-omelette.note: 3 eggs per omelette in an 8-inch nonstick pan, with ham, pepper and onion cooked first and the omelette folded over cheese: the same build and pan size as published versions.

white-bean-and-rosemary-dip.note: Two cans of cannellini blended with garlic and rosemary warmed in oil, the juice of a lemon and 2–4 tbsp water. Sunset and Coley Cooks use the same two-can base with lemon, rosemary and a little water or oil.

white-bean-tomato-and-spinach-pasta.note: Garlic oil, burst cherry tomatoes, cannellini and wilted spinach, finished with lemon, Parmesan and pasta water: the published Tuscan-style method.

white-bean-turkey-chili.note: Ground turkey, 3 cans cannellini (some mashed), 3 cups broth, cumin, finished with cream cheese and lime; published versions use 3 cans to 3-4 cups broth and the same creamy finish. No change.

zucchini-bread.note: One 9x5 loaf with 2 cups flour, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup oil and 2 cups grated zucchini matches published single loaves (1 3/4–2 cups flour, 1/2 cup oil, 2 eggs). Baking powder plus soda is in range, and 55–65 minutes at 350°F matches their 55–70.

zucchini-fritters.note: Works: zucchini salted 10 min and squeezed, about 0.4 cup flour per lb, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 3-4 min a side. PROVENANCE: close to Once Upon a Chef's feta-dill fritters (same 2 eggs, 2 tbsp dill, 1/2 cup feta, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 10-min salting, same order). Ours differs in zucchini (1 1/4 lb), flour (1/2 cup), oil and the added yogurt sauce. Left as is.

rework.matched: Once Upon a Chef's zucchini fritters with feta and dill (2 eggs, 2 tbsp dill, 1/2 c feta, 1/4 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp BP, 10-min salting)
rework.changed: zucchini 1 1/4 → 1 1/2 lb (3 medium); flour 1/2 → 2/3 cup; baking powder 1/2 → 1 tsp; feta 1/2 → 3/4 cup; green onions 3 → 4; dill 2 → 3 tbsp; pepper 1/4 → 1/2 tsp; salting 10 → 15 min with 3/4 tsp salt (no salt in the batter now); lemon 1/2 → 1, its zest goes into the fritters and the juice into the sauce, the rest served as wedges; method: dry ingredients whisked first, zucchini and add-ins tossed in them, beaten eggs stirred in last (Once Upon a Chef adds flour last); oil 1/4 → 1/3 cup, 3 tbsp to start; about 20 fritters; prep 20 → 30, cook 20 → 25 min; tagline rewritten. Kept: 2 eggs, 2 garlic cloves, yogurt sauce.
rework.note: Per pound of zucchini, published versions use 1/4-1/2 cup flour (Once Upon a Chef and NC State 1/4, Natasha 3/8, Saveur about 0.42, Foodiecrush 1/2; ours 0.44), 1 1/3-2 tsp baking powder per cup of flour (ours 1 1/2), 1-2 eggs, 1/3-2/3 cup feta (ours 1/2), and salt for 10-30 min before squeezing (NC State 15-30, Kaiser 10-15). Heaping 2-tbsp fritters fried 3-5 min a side over medium is standard.
